evidence.title: 《日下舊聞考》 on 劉猛將軍廟
evidence.excerpt_zh: 月地雲居之東為法源樓又東為静室西度橋折而北為劉猛將軍廟
evidence.summary: The temple to the locust-quelling god, north over a bridge from the area of 月地云居.

evidence.title: Scene 15, 山高水长 Shangao Shuichang, the Drill Field
evidence.excerpt_other: The largest open field in the Yuan Ming Yuan was near the southwest corner of the garden. On the east side stood a two-story building from which the Emperor, his officials, and the ladies of the court could view the archery contests,
evidence.summary: Largest open field, with a two-storey viewing building on the east, used for archery, feasts for embassies and fireworks. Dutch embassy here January-February 1795. Across the stream a half-mile straight horse run from the round tower in the north to 藻园 in the south; by the round tower a small shrine to General Liu Meng (per Jung Hua).

evidence.title: 贾珺 on 刘猛将军庙
evidence.summary: Three-bay hall with ridge and finials in a small walled forecourt, under 2 zhang deep; appears on the Forty Scenes album. Repaired 1793. Yongzheng spread the cult against locusts. The plaques 昆虫毋作, 用佐为霖 near 安佑宫 may belong to it.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
